title: Align Copies to Surface Normal
prompt: Orient instances so they stand up along each point's surface normal
explanation: dihedral() returns the quaternion that rotates the first vector onto the second, so this aligns each instance's local up-axis to the surface normal. Copy to Points (and the USD Instancer) read p@orient directly, making this the canonical way to plant objects on a surface.

title: Scale Points by Neighbour Density
prompt: Make points smaller where the point cloud is denser
explanation: pcopen() opens a point cloud query around @P within a radius and pcnumfound() returns how many points it found. fit() inverts that count into a size, so crowded regions get small points and sparse regions get large ones. Always pcclose() the handle.

title: Random Colour per Connected Piece
prompt: Give every connected piece a unique random colour
explanation: A Connectivity SOP labels each disconnected piece with an integer i@class. Feeding that integer (scaled to decorrelate it) into rand() produces a deterministic random colour per piece -- the standard way to visualise fracture or scatter groupings.

title: Connect Points into a Polyline
prompt: Build a single open polyline through all input points
explanation: Running in detail (once) mode, this creates one polyline primitive and appends a vertex referencing each point number in turn. It is the VEX equivalent of an Add SOP's 'by group' polyline mode, but fully procedural and reorderable.

title: Ridged fBm Displacement along Normal
prompt: Displace a surface along its normal with layered ridged noise
explanation: Each octave doubles frequency and halves amplitude; taking abs() of the noise creates sharp ridges instead of smooth hills. The summed value drives displacement along the normalised normal, a classic procedural-terrain pattern.

title: Cull Points Beyond a Radius
prompt: Delete points farther than a given distance from the origin
explanation: length(@P) is the distance from the origin; points beyond the radius are deleted with removepoint(). Because removepoint runs safely per-point in a wrangle, this is a cheap procedural clip with no group bookkeeping.

title: Curvature Mask from Neighbour Normals
prompt: Estimate surface curvature by comparing a point's normal to its neighbours
explanation: neighbours() returns the connected point indices; averaging their normals gives the local mean orientation. The dot product between that average and this point's normal is ~1 on flat areas and drops on curved areas, so 1 - dot is a handy curvature/edge-wear mask.

title: Arc-Length Parameter along a Polyline
prompt: Write a normalized arc-length u value along each polyline's points
explanation: primpoints() gives the ordered points of each primitive. A first pass sums total length; a second pass writes the running fraction as curveu via setpointattrib(). Unlike the Resample SOP's curveu, this works without resampling and preserves the original points.

title: Per-Copy Variation for Copy to Points
prompt: Randomize orientation, scale and colour per instance for Copy to Points
explanation: Each call to rand() with a distinct seed offset yields an independent stream, so orientation, scale and colour vary without correlating. quaternion(angle, axis) spins each copy about Y; fit01 maps the unit random into a size range.

title: Snap Positions to a Grid
prompt: Quantize point positions onto a regular grid for welding
explanation: Dividing by the cell size, rounding, and multiplying back snaps positions to a lattice. This is the standard pre-pass before a Fuse to merge near-coincident geometry onto exact shared points.
